title: M12.1: machining mesh - crafted records that provoke every solidcore-tess shortfall, and a proven deviation bound for spline faces

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Follow-up of #940 (machining mesh seam, PR stacked on #941).

What #940 delivers: `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh` refuses by name every `PlanStats` shortfall that touches the guarantee (unmeshed, lenient, unsampled edge, a face or edge capped off its tolerance), pinned by `every_planner_shortfall_is_a_refusal_or_a_note` on SYNTHETIC `PlanStats` values; and a SAMPLED deviation (15 barycentric points a triangle), judged by the closed-form distance to the record's analytic surface where the face is analytic, else by the parametric distance |S(u,v) - T(u,v)|.

Owed:
1. **Real provocations.** No fixture under testdata/models makes the planner report any shortfall (checked at 0.005, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0002 and 0.0001 mm on Milling-test.step and sample_ap214.step). Build small crafted records (a pcurve off its edge, a free edge, a face whose grid must be thinned past `MAX_FACE_GRID`, an edge past 20 000 nodes) and pin that each reaches its named `MeshRefusal` through `machining_mesh`, not only through `judge_stats`.
2. **Spline and revolved faces.** They are judged only by the parametric distance, which over-reads on a non-uniform parameterisation (a few per cent on a rational circle) - a possible false refusal. Add a projection onto the plan surface (Newton from the sample's (u, v)) so they get a true distance, with a fixture that has such a face.
3. **Between the samples.** The deviation is a sampled maximum, a lower bound of the true one; solidcore-tess meshes right up to the tolerance (0.993 of it on Milling-test). Either a stated bound on the sag between samples, or a margin in the seam, so "within" is a guarantee.

What upstream solidcore-tess would need (for the maintainer to raise; not filed upstream): a cancellation hook in `plan`; a per-face measured sag in `PlanStats` for every face; a stated bound on the sag between the planner's sample points.

Everything stays inside `crates/kernel`. Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: each shortfall entry is pinned by a crafted record through `machining_mesh`; a non-analytic face is judged by a projected distance with a fixture; the decision file says what bounds the sag between samples.
